newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Evening Standard - May 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Evening Standard - May 7.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company

A report out today from the Broadcasting Standards Commission, finds that parents believe television encourages bad behaviour, and viewers and listeners in general believe broadcasters should be regulated for the common good. The report says "Parents in particular saw television as anti-authority, believing that it condoned unsociable behaviour such as swearing".
- ACCOUNTING GIANT TO STAKE AILING FIRMS

Price Waterhouse has announced that it will take equity stakes in ailing companies which it is called in to turn around. The firm also proposes setting up a quasi-venture capital fund, backed by partners' money, to invest in the businesses it advises.
- HOPES HIGH AS DOW SCALES NEW PEAKS

London dealers have high hopes of another good day, following a volatile session on Wall Street in which the Dow Jones Industrial Average shot up 10.83 points to a fresh all-time high of 7225.32. However, the market will be closely watching two sets of economic figures from the US: March wholesale inventories and first- quarter productivity.
- MEGA WORKLOAD FOR NEW TRADE SUPREMO

Margaret Beckett, the new President of the Board of Trade, has a barrage of reports from the Monopolies and Mergers Commission which require her attention, concerning anything from price- fixing to mega-mergers. Among cases waiting for a deicision are British Airways' proposal to merge with American Airlines, and Bass' proposal to buy Allied Domecq's half share in Carlsberg Tetley.
